rationale: Iteration 0 has no race data, so this is a conservative baseline. Geometry: five line sensors spread across the 0.04 m width (x = -0.02 to +0.02) at y = 0.04 m ahead of the axle. That gives enough coverage to track a 25 mm tape and see its centre. Sensor size is 0.008 m for fine position resolution. Wheel track 0.12 m and radius 0.03 m give a moderate turn rate. Mass 0.8 kg and body 0.12 x 0.18 m keep the yaw inertia moderate and the off-track limit (max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) m) reasonable. Controller: base_speed 1.8 (PWM about 90% of full) to target the ~1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s while leaving some margin for turns. Sensor weights are linear across the array (-1, -0.5, 0, 0.5, 1) so the signal is proportional to lateral offset. kp = 4 gives roughly 1400 PWM of differential for a full-scale signal. ki = 0 avoids integral windup on curves. kd = 0.1 adds mild damping. line_loss = last_direction so the robot searches toward the side it last saw the tape. Expected result: completes the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. If steering_oscillation is high, reduce kp or raise kd. If the robot drifts wide on bends, raise kp. If it cannot finish in time, raise base_speed. Hypotheses to check: (1) the robot completes all three development tracks; (2) rms_error stays under about 0.02 m; (3) line_loss_events are 0 or 1.
